summary: Wrote three plain-English concept pages for the research console: 'What makes a board good?' (the fair leaf evaluator x-rayed on an engine-produced position, with the terms that survive grouped by the finding-13 in-leaf profile and a look-alike board pair demonstrating that static board potential is insufficient), 'Score is survival' (one complete toy-policy game as a timeline, the 17,000-point rise economy, and the 2.4 clears / 1.4 reveals per move flow balance quoted from status.md as diagnostic targets from limited runs), and 'Why one great game proves nothing' (the per-game scores of the retained 64-game fair-D4 cohort from finding-01 as a strip plot, mean versus median, paired cohorts, and bootstrap lower bounds). Added the server-component figure module web/components/ConceptsB.tsx and four data-generation scripts that use the TypeScript engine in latent mode on playground seeds; every board shown is engine output and every research number is quoted from a retained record with its evidence label. No research record, protocol or source file was modified and no gameplay experiment was run.
limitations: Self-reported contribution; not yet independently reviewed.
